Assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:
- Policy stance: Strongly accommodative at the zero lower bound with ongoing Treasury and agency MBS/CMBS purchases, active repo and ON RRP operations, and symmetric 2% inflation objective—supportive of market functioning and credit availability.
- SLOOS credit conditions: Banks reported broad-based tightening of lending standards and terms for C&I (all firm sizes) and CRE, and tighter standards for household credit (credit card, auto, and even residential mortgages), driven by reduced risk tolerance and concerns about the economic outlook and collateral values. Loan demand was generally weaker for C&I and CRE; mortgage demand was stronger (especially refi) but faced tighter standards. Banks anticipated maintaining tighter standards in the near term.
- FSR context on risks: COVID-19 continues to weigh on activity and inflation; vulnerabilities elevated in SMEs/households; nonbank servicer and CRE strains; sectoral stress (energy, airlines, leisure). March 2020 funding dislocations have eased with policy support but remain shock-sensitive.
- Backstops and market functioning: Facilities and asset purchases (CPFF, SMCCF, MLF, TALF, FIMA repo, swap lines) helped restore functioning and temper downside risks.

Net tone: Cautiously negative, and more so than previously assessed, as SLOOS signals tighter bank credit supply and weaker loan demand that may dampen policy transmission despite strong Fed backstops and improved market functioning.
